source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Share an adult bed with the infant overnight so the parent can continuously monitor breathing","B":"Use pillows and thick blankets in the sleep space to prevent the infant from becoming cold","C":"Avoid smoke and overheating and consider a pacifier for sleep once breastfeeding is established","D":"Permit secondhand smoke exposure because tobacco smoke is not associated with sleep-related death"}}
source_row.rationale: In addition to safe sleep positioning (back to sleep, firm surface), comprehensive SIDS risk reduction education includes avoiding infant exposure to smoke, offering a pacifier at sleep time (once breastfeeding is well-established, generally around 3-4 weeks), and avoiding overheating/overbundling the infant — all evidence-based recommendations from the AAP, while bed-sharing is not recommended.
source_row.source_detail: AAP safe-sleep recommendations: smoke avoidance, pacifier at sleep, avoid overheating and bed-sharing; reviewed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: American Academy of Pediatrics — SIDS Risk Reduction Recommendations
source_row.stem: A nurse is providing SIDS (Sudden Infant Death Syndrome) risk reduction education to new parents. In addition to safe sleep positioning, the nurse should include which additional recommendation?
